patients.label: 56-year-old Hispanic man with lung cancer treated with high dose intravenous vitamin C

identity_evidence.quote: A case of a 56 year old male Hispanic patient

attribution_limitations: Timing inconsistency: vitamin C infusions are stated to start in December 2013, but the August 2013 CEA sentence says the improvement occurred while high doses of vitamin C infusions were given, and the abstract says CEA stayed normal while the infusions were given.

Adjuvant therapy duration: the case report places docetaxel and carboplatin from about week 7 to week 20 post-operative, whereas the discussion says adjuvant therapy lasted just 27 weeks after the surgery.
Unclear whether the chemotherapy with last cycle in November 2013 is the same course as the adjuvant docetaxel and carboplatin completed in week 20 post-operative.
Nodule wording is ambiguous: "two nodules in the left mid lung and the other in the right upper lobe" does not make the total count clear.
CEA unit differs: the August 2013 value is printed as ng/mg while other CEA values are ng/mL.
The chest CT date is not stated; it follows the November 2012 laboratory sentence ("also performed") but carries no date of its own.
The G6PD test result is not stated; the next sentence says the patient showed no problem handling the IV vitamin C.
The discussion states laboratory values were within normal levels except for CEA, AST and ALT without a time; which measurement time(s) it summarizes is not stated.

limitations: No figures or supplements are listed in the source.
Lung cancer histology and stage are not stated.
The abstract conclusion that vitamin C had no secondary effects is a study-level claim and is not recorded as an adverse-event fact.
The undated discussion sentence that laboratory values were within normal levels except for CEA, AST and ALT is kept review_only.
Vitamin C start date (December 2013) conflicts in timing with the August 2013 CEA sentence; see ambiguities.

claims.text: A 56-year-old Hispanic man with a history of chronic smoking and associated COPD has been diagnosed with lung cancer since 2012. In November 2012 CEA 6.5 ng/mL, AST 44 u/L and ALT 77 u/L were elevated, and chest CT showed calcifications of the coronary arteries and lung nodules. In March 2013 ALT was 67 u/L and CEA 13 ng/mL, both elevated.
